n1.notes: Refarmed 3G/4G core band; widely deployed for 5G NSA/SA coverage layers in Europe and Asia.

n3.notes: Most common LTE band globally, increasingly refarmed to NR via DSS.

n5.notes: Low-band coverage layer in the Americas and Oceania.

n7.notes: Mid-band capacity layer, common in Europe, LATAM and Canada.

n25.notes: Superset of PCS; used by T-Mobile/Sprint heritage networks in the US.

n28.notes: Primary 5G coverage band in Europe, APAC and LATAM; excellent indoor penetration.

n38.notes: TDD slice inside the 2.6 GHz IMT-E gap; used in Europe.

n40.notes: Capacity band in India, China, and parts of APAC.

n41.notes: T-Mobile US 'Ultra Capacity' workhorse and China Mobile's primary 5G band; up to 100 MHz carriers.

n48.notes: US shared-spectrum (CBRS) band, popular for private 5G networks.

n66.notes: North American mid-band; superset of LTE Band 4.

n71.notes: T-Mobile US 'Extended Range 5G' low-band coverage layer.

n75.notes: Supplemental downlink band used in Europe.

n77.notes: Superset of n78; includes US C-Band (3.7–3.98 GHz) and Japan's 3.3–4.2 GHz allocations.

n78.notes: The most widely deployed 5G mid-band worldwide; the global capacity workhorse.

n79.notes: Used in China, Japan and Russia; often absent from devices sold in the Americas/Europe.

n261.notes: Verizon's original 5G Ultra Wideband band; subset of n257.

b1.notes: Original WCDMA core band, ubiquitous outside the Americas.

b3.notes: The most deployed LTE band in the world.

b4.notes: North American AWS; largely subsumed by B66.

glossary.SSB: Synchronization Signal Block — the PSS + SSS + PBCH bundle a UE searches for during cell acquisition; placed on the synchronization raster addressed by GSCN.
glossary.GSCN: Global Synchronization Channel Number — index on the synchronization raster that defines where SSBs may be placed (TS 38.104 §5.4.3).
glossary.ARFCN: Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number — integer index on the global frequency raster identifying an RF reference frequency (TS 38.104 §5.4.2).
glossary.BWP: Bandwidth Part — a contiguous subset of a carrier's resource blocks that a UE can be configured to operate in, enabling power savings and mixed numerologies.
glossary.CA: Carrier Aggregation — combining multiple component carriers to increase bandwidth and throughput.
glossary.DSS: Dynamic Spectrum Sharing — running LTE and NR simultaneously in the same carrier by scheduling them on a per-subframe basis.
glossary.SCS: Subcarrier Spacing — OFDM subcarrier width; 15/30/60 kHz in FR1, 60/120 kHz in FR2; set by numerology mu (SCS = 15 * 2^mu kHz).
glossary.TDD: Time Division Duplex — uplink and downlink share one frequency, separated in time by a slot format pattern.
glossary.FDD: Frequency Division Duplex — uplink and downlink use separate paired frequencies simultaneously.
glossary.NSA: Non-Standalone — 5G NR anchored to an LTE core (EN-DC); the first deployment mode of 5G.
glossary.SA: Standalone — 5G NR with a 5G core (5GC), enabling slicing, lower latency, and VoNR.
glossary.MIMO: Multiple Input Multiple Output — spatial multiplexing across antenna layers; peak NR DL is 8 layers, typically 4 in commercial FR1 networks.
glossary.PRB: Physical Resource Block — 12 consecutive subcarriers; the basic unit of frequency-domain scheduling.
glossary.EN-DC: E-UTRAN New Radio Dual Connectivity — the NSA architecture where a UE connects to LTE (anchor) and NR simultaneously.
glossary.NR-DC: New Radio Dual Connectivity — a UE connects to two NR cell groups at once, typically an FR1 master (e.g. n78) plus an FR2 secondary (e.g. n258/n260), combining coverage with mmWave capacity.
glossary.VoNR: Voice over New Radio — IMS voice carried natively over a 5G SA connection.
glossary.5G: Fifth-generation cellular — defined by 3GPP NR (New Radio) in FR1 (sub-6 GHz) and FR2 (mmWave), supporting SA (5G core) and NSA (EN-DC with LTE anchor) deployment.
